title: InSight Crime: CJNG's 'Operadores Droneros' Unit Has Extended Weaponized Drone Attacks to Five Mexican States
detail: Infobae reported August 26, 2026 on an InSight Crime investigation into CJNG's dedicated drone warfare unit, known internally as 'Operadores Droneros' and identifiable by a circular skull patch, established around 2020. The unit adapts commercially available drones — rather than manufacturing its own, per InSight Crime co-director Jeremy McDermott — to drop explosive devices on security forces, vehicles, and buildings; ferry improvised explosive devices; deliver chemical-substance payloads causing respiratory harm; and, in at least one documented case, attack a military helicopter using combined gunfire and an IED. InSight Crime identified weaponized-drone activity attributed to the unit across five states: Michoacán, Guanajuato, Chihuahua, Jalisco, and Baja California, with footage distributed on social media for intimidation purposes. The report noted smaller organizations, including Cárteles Unidos and Los Ardillos, have also adopted drone tactics, and referenced an August 17, 2026 Mexico-U.S. cooperation agreement on counter-drone technology, though experts cautioned that drones' widespread legitimate commercial uses make market-level interdiction impractical.

media.caption: InSight Crime investigation into CJNG's 'Operadores Droneros' unit and its weaponized-drone reach across five Mexican states

confidenceReason: Based on InSight Crime's independent investigative reporting and analyst assessment (Jeremy McDermott); specific incident attributions to the named unit have not been independently confirmed by Mexican federal authorities.
